system_description.narrative_title: Iran war destabilizes global energy markets and geopolitics
system_description.narrative_summary: A widening conflict centered on Iran, its proxies (notably the Houthis) and Gulf states — and the U.S. role — is disrupting oil production, exports and shipping (pipeline strikes, Hormuz bottlenecks and ship-to-ship transfers), driving price volatility and large economic costs for households and governments. The military and diplomatic responses (arms sales, interceptor use, meetings in Oman/China/UN) and collateral impacts (cyberattacks, cloud outages, refugee/humanitarian crises, regional spillovers into Lebanon, Gaza and Yemen) create reinforcing feedbacks that amplify supply shocks, financial market moves and political polarization.
system_description.scope: Inside: state and non-state actors in the Iran-Gulf conflict (Iran, Houthis, Saudi Arabia, UAE, US, Israel, Gulf states), oil production/export infrastructure (East-West pipeline, tankers, Hormuz transit), global oil markets and prices, financial markets (stocks/bonds), military logistics and munitions inventories, diplomatic negotiations, cyber/cloud infrastructure in the Gulf, and near-term humanitarian impacts and refugee flows. Variables include supply disruptions, freight routes, oil price, household energy costs, munitions stock levels, diplomatic engagement, and cyber-resilience.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-economic system (energy markets, international trade, finance, and security architectures)
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and investor sentiment
Global logistics, shipping and refinery supply chains
Regional humanitarian and security subsystem (Gaza, Lebanon, Yemen)
Technology and cybersecurity infrastructure (cloud providers, maritime cyber)

variables.name: Physical oil supply level
variables.description: The aggregated available volume of crude oil and refined products physically available for global markets at a given time.

variables.name: Oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price per barrel of crude oil expressed as a continuous market price metric.

variables.name: Oil price volatility
variables.description: The short- to medium-term variability or dispersion of oil prices measured as a continuous volatility metric.

variables.name: Shipping chokepoint transit capacity
variables.description: The maximum continuous throughput of maritime crude and product shipments that can transit critical narrow sea routes.

variables.name: Pipeline operational capacity
variables.description: The aggregate functional throughput capacity of overland oil export pipelines, accounting for damage and repairs.

variables.name: Tanker fleet utilization rate
variables.description: The proportion of the available tanker fleet actively engaged in transport or under transit relative to total fleet capacity.

variables.name: Strategic reserve level
variables.description: The aggregated quantity of emergency crude and fuel held in strategic stockpiles available to mitigate supply shocks.

variables.name: Refinery operational capacity
variables.description: The effective processing capacity of refineries able to convert crude into refined products given outages and maintenance.

variables.name: Household energy cost burden
variables.description: The average share of household income spent on energy and transport fuels, measured continuously across households.

variables.name: Government fiscal pressure level
variables.description: The degree of fiscal strain on public budgets measured by deficits, emergency spending needs and revenue shortfalls.

variables.name: Munitions inventory level
variables.description: The aggregated stock of deployable munitions, interceptors and expendable ordnance available to armed forces.

variables.name: Military engagement intensity
variables.description: The rate and scale of kinetic and offensive military actions occurring in the conflict theatre measured continuously.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement activity
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of sustained diplomatic negotiations, mediation efforts and multilateral interactions.

variables.name: Cloud service availability
variables.description: The operational availability and reliability of regional cloud and critical IT services supporting commerce and logistics.

variables.name: Forced displacement flow rate
variables.description: The continuous flow rate of people being displaced or seeking refuge as a result of conflict and related disruptions.

variables.name: Financial market risk premium
variables.description: The incremental cost of capital reflected in spreads, insurance rates and required returns due to heightened geopolitical risk.

catalysts.title: World leaders convene at UNGA
catalysts.description: UN General Assembly meetings and side talks where leaders (including US and Iranian delegations) may push ceasefire, sanctions or de-escalation deals.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Why are world leaders at the UN next week'; 'US to allow Iranian leaders to attend UN General Assembly'.

catalysts.title: Saudi East‑West pipeline partly restored
catalysts.description: Saudi officials and US energy secretary indicate the damaged East‑West pipeline could be back online within days, restoring exports.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US energy chief says Saudi Arabia oil pipeline should be back online within days'; 'Saudi cancels some oil cargoes after pipeline hit'.

catalysts.title: Escalating Houthi-Saudi strikes
catalysts.description: Continued Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure and shipping, and reciprocal Saudi coalition strikes, intensify disruptions across the Gulf.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Saudis and Houthis exchange strikes'; 'Three pumping stations along Saudi East‑West Pipeline were hit'; 'Houthi blitz leaves Saudi Arabia exposed'.

catalysts.title: Aramco boosts Gulf exports Sept–Oct
catalysts.description: Aramco plans temporary export increases in September–October via alternative loadings and Hormuz routing to offset pipeline disruption.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Aramco to boost Gulf exports to 60 million barrels in September, October'; 'Saudi offers more crude via Oman loading after pipeline attacks'.

catalysts.title: U.S. clears fighter jet sale to Saudi Arabia
catalysts.description: U.S. advances/clears approvals for a $24.3bn fighter jet (and related munitions) sale to Saudi Arabia, altering regional military stocks.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US clears way for $24.3 billion fighter jet sale to Saudi Arabia'; 'US to allow Iranian leaders to attend UN General Assembly' (diplomatic context).

catalysts.title: Ongoing AWS outages in Gulf data zones
catalysts.description: Amazon AWS reports inability to restore some Bahrain/UAE data after strikes, leaving cloud services degraded in the Gulf for months.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'AWS says it can't restore service to Bahrain, UAE facilities 6 months after Iran strikes'; 'AWS says it can't restore some data'.

catalysts.title: Iran activates land trade routes
catalysts.description: Iran is activating/expanding overland trade routes to bypass maritime/blockade routes, partially restoring commerce and reducing sea-dependence.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Iran activates land routes to bypass US blockade'; 'Iran Struggles to Shift Trade to Land'.

catalysts.title: Yemen offensive drives displacement
catalysts.description: Houthi advances and Saudi-Houthi exchanges force new waves of internal displacement and refugee flows from Yemen.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Yemen conflict displaces 112,000 people'; 'Barefoot and terrified, Yemenis flee the Houthi advance'.

catalysts.title: Interceptor and munitions depletion
catalysts.description: U.S. and allied forces are rapidly using interceptors and munitions, creating shortfalls that affect air defence and strike capacity.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'The U.S. Is Burning Through Its Supply of Interceptors'; 'Trump’s Iran war has caused munitions “shortfall”'.

catalysts.title: Surge in supertanker orders
catalysts.description: Shipowners place large supertanker orders to hedge against Gulf disruptions, expanding future transport capacity over months.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US-Iran conflict helps drive wave of supertanker orders'.
